name: Egg Soufflé
description: Historical recipe from The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Cream the butter, add flour, and pour on gradually scalded milk and cream.
Cook in double boiler five minutes, and add yolks of eggs, beaten until thick and lemon-colored.
Remove from fire, add seasonings, and fold in whites of eggs beaten until stiff and dry.
Turn into a buttered dish, or buttered individual moulds, set in pan of hot water, and bake in a slow oven until firm.
Egg Soufflé may be served with White Sauce I, highly seasoned with celery salt, paprika, and onion juice.

source.author: Fannie Merritt Farmer
source.originalInstructions:
1. Cream the butter, add flour, and pour on gradually scalded milk and cream.
2. Cook in double boiler five minutes, and add yolks of eggs, beaten until thick and lemon-colored.
3. Remove from fire, add seasonings, and fold in whites of eggs beaten until stiff and dry.
4. Turn into a buttered dish, or buttered individual moulds, set in pan of hot water, and bake in a slow oven until firm.
5. Egg Soufflé may be served with White Sauce I, highly seasoned with celery salt, paprika, and onion juice.
